messages:
ashley: Heads up — I pushed a proposal to harden TLS profiles on edge proxies: blocklist RC4, 3DES, TLS1.0/1.1, and enable TLS1.3-only for internal-e2e paths. Planning a staged rollout across eu, na, ap regions.

ben: copying the draft now. main risk is older customer SDKs + some legacy partners that still talk TLS1.0. Also KMS IAM change last week tightened decrypt permissions on the proxy keystore role — saw 503s in canaries earlier.

maria: is the 503 from KMS decrypt denies or from TLS handshake failures? I saw a flurry of authz denies around 03:12 UTC in the audit logs.

liam: audit logs show two concurrent issues: (1) keystore-service returning KMS::AccessDenied for a subset of proxy pods after the RBAC scope tightening, (2) proxies failing cipher negotiation for clients that advertise old suites. Both surfaced same window.

ashley: thanks. we need to avoid coupling the TLS profile rollout to the RBAC change. rollback plan: revert TLS profile change if KMS errors persist, or revert RBAC tightening if we can't get decrypt to stable state in 30m.

devops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-2435 - proxy-keystore-decrypt-failures (severity: P2). Pager duty channel: @oncall-sre.

oncall-bot: oncall rotation: sam (primary), liam (secondary).

sam: pinged SRE/keystore team. quick check: `gcloud kms keys describe projects/redwood/locations/global/keyR` shows key exists and IAM bindings were last modified 2d ago.

maria: i can patch the keystore to retry KMS unwrap with exponential backoff and log full request IDs. but that won't fix an IAM deny. we need a policy audit: what principal did we give decrypt to?

liam: confirmed: deploy 2026-03-14 tightened `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to `serviceAccount:keystore@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` but our proxy pods use `edge-proxy-sa@redwood....` The keystore service had assumed the keystore SA previously via impersonation; that path was removed.

ben: ok — two immediate remediation options: (A) restore impersonation role-binding for keystore so existing flow works, or (B) rotate the proxies to new flow where they call keystore as keystore-sa via signed tokens. A is fastest.

ashley: agree. A as hotfix to clear customer impact, but we must record why impersonation is a weaker pattern. We'll follow with B as secure-lab migration. Schedule: hotfix now, full migration within 2 weeks with rollout plan & evals.

maria: for the TLS hardening rollout, recommend canary in na-west restricted to internal-services tag and 30s failure threshold. Also add telemetry to capture `TLSVersion` and `CipherSuite` per-connection in traces so we can quantify clients impacted.

sam: i can wire a quick Grafana panel: edge.tls.connections by tls_version, cipher, region. Add alert if >1% connections fail handshake post-change.

liam: one more gotcha — OCSP stapling TTLs. If we flip to TLS1.3-only and some cert stapling responses expire, spikes in OCSP fetches could cascade to latency. please add rate-limiter on stapling fetches in front of CA/OCSP cache.

ashley: noted. also add a pre-rollout test: run synthetic clients that emulate oldest supported SDKs (java-8-legacy, python-requests-2.7, old-go-tls). If any fail handshake against canary, abort.

ben: about audit logs: the RBAC change removed a serviceAccount binding — we should add an automated post-change checklist: (1) confirm KMS decrypt success on 5 sample pods per region, (2) check audit logs for `cryptoKeyVersions.access` denies, (3) sanity-check telemetry for handshake failures.

maria: i'll author the checklist and post as runbook PR. also include a step to snapshot IAM bindings and push to `infra-audit` bucket (encrypted).

devops-bot: deploy pipeline:edge-proxy-tls-profile v2 → canary na-west started by ashley at 6372119001.

sam: quick note — don't enable TLS1.3-only for external customer-facing endpoints until opt-in; some enterprise customers expect legacy ciphers. internal-e2e first, then partner opt-in, then public opt-out.

ashley: correct. internal-e2e first, then partner opt-in, then public opt-out. communication plan: email to customer-success + a banner on dashboard about upcoming TLS deprecations with migration docs.

liam: migration tasks for security/infra: update keystore impersonation hotfix (rollback window 60m), add KMS role audit, update proxy TLS config templates, create canary job for legacy SDKs.

ben: vulnerability triage: blocklisting RC4/3DES/TLS1.0/1.1 reduces CVE exposure surface. mark the change as mitigates CVE-2016-2183 etc in the ticket.

maria: PR for runbook incoming in ~30m. will include playbook steps to revert RBAC or TLS profile and commands:```\
# restore impersonation binding\
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding keystore@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\
  --member="serviceAccount:edge-proxy-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \\
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"\
\n# check KMS decrypt on a pod\
kubectl exec -n edge $(kubectl get pods -l app=edge-proxy -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- \\
  curl -sS -X POST http://keystore.internal/unwrap -d '{"key_id":"projects/..."}' | jq .
```

sam: thanks, will hook alerts. once hotfix is in, we flip canary TLS profile and monitor for 15m then proceed.

ashley: owners: hotfix — liam, runbook — maria, canary rollout — sam. I'll do the customer comms draft. any objections? :thumbsup: :thumbsdown:

ben: :thumbsup:

liam: :thumbsup:

maria: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

ashley: deploying hotfix now. will update thread with timestamps and postmortem link if anything unusual.
